summary: Iteration 21 — Guest Mode (net-new): full backend + frontend verification. VERDICT: ALL PASS, ZERO REGRESSIONS. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests green (test_iteration21_guest_mode.py) covering (1) POST /api/auth/guest mints guest_-prefixed session + is_guest:true user + 'Guest' name + @guest.aureve.local email; (2) GET /api/auth/me returns {is_guest:true, premium:false, trial_eligible:true, trial_used:false}; (3) scoped data endpoints — GET /api/profiles auto-creates a default individual profile for the guest, POST /api/items (name+category+photo) succeeds and GET /api/items returns the item, POST /api/outfits succeeds and GET /api/outfits returns it; (4) FREE-tier gating — POST /api/stylist/suggest on first call is NOT 402 (metered 5/day), and all Premium-only features return HTTP 402 for the guest: /dressme, /packing/plan, /capsule/build, /insights/health-report, /insights/missing-piece, /tryon, /shop-check; also /api/profiles second-profile creation returns 402 (household is premium); (5) /auth/session compatibility — seeded bearer test-session-token-aura-123 still resolves to user_testaura01 via /auth/me (auth pipeline unbroken), POST /auth/session with a bogus session_token still returns 401 (no 500), and passing guest_token='' or a non-existent 'guest_...' string does NOT crash the endpoint (still 401 from Emergent, migrate is guarded); (6) POST /auth/logout with a guest bearer deletes the session (subsequent /auth/me → 401). Frontend (390x844 mobile viewport, real preview URL): /login shows both testID google-login-button (Continue with Google) AND testID guest-login-button (Explore as guest); tapping Explore as guest calls POST /api/auth/guest (guest_-prefixed token stashed in localStorage under aura_session_token) and lands in (tabs) Home which renders 'Good afternoon', a Dress Me hero WITH LOCK ICON (nice free-tier cue), Recent Outfits empty state, and Quick Actions (Add Item / Create Outfit / AI Stylist / My Collections). Bottom tab bar navigation for the guest works cleanly across all 5 tabs — Home /, Wardrobe /wardrobe (empty 'Your wardrobe is a blank canvas' + 'Add first piece'), Dress Me /dressme (correctly redirects to /premium paywall since guest=free), Outfits /outfits ('My Outfits' + empty state), Profile /profile — no red screens, no console errors beyond the pre-existing app-wide RN-Web deprecation warnings (shadow*, props.pointerEvents) inherited from prior iterations. Profile screen for the guest matches spec exactly: avatar 'G' + name 'Guest' + 'Guest mode' badge; the ugly @guest.aureve.local email is HIDDEN (verified in DOM innerText); testID logout-button is NOT present for guests (verified is_visible=False); testID guest-backup-cta IS visible with 'Back up your wardrobe' / 'You're exploring as a guest. Sign in with Google and everything you've added moves to your account.' — tapping it invokes the same login() flow which stashes the guest token in secure storage under aura_guest_migrate_token so /auth/session can pass it back for migration. migrate_guest_data was already unit-tested by main agent against DB (profiles reassigned, items follow via profile_id, usage migrated, guest+sessions deleted); we validated the surrounding pipeline (guest_token stash, /auth/session accepts optional guest_token without breaking, seeded token still works).
critical_code_review_comments: Trial eligibility for guests: /auth/me returns trial_eligible:true for guests. If a guest starts a 7-day trial (POST /api/trial/start likely sets premium_until on the guest user_id), then later signs in with Google, migrate_guest_data reassigns profiles + usage to the new account_id but does NOT copy premium_until/trial_used off the guest user before deleting it. Net effect: the trial silently disappears on sign-in and the user could start ANOTHER trial on the real account. Consider either (a) hiding trial CTAs while is_guest=true, or (b) copying premium_until/premium_source/trial_used onto the target account inside migrate_guest_data (only if the target doesn't already have equal-or-better entitlement).

migrate_guest_data does not delete guest wardrobe if the guest_token is expired/deleted before /auth/session runs (early return on session lookup miss). Minor — 7-day TTL makes this rare, but worth logging when it happens so the main agent can decide whether to run a periodic cleanup of orphan guest users.

Guest session token is stored under the same key (aura_session_token) as a signed-in account — losing localStorage or being pushed off by another sign-in on the same browser will silently drop unmigrated guest data. Consider a subtle 'You have unsaved wardrobe changes' warning if the app boots and finds a guest_-prefixed token AND the user is about to log in from a fresh flow (defence-in-depth beyond the current stashGuestToken).
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run mints ~2 guest users via POST /api/auth/guest and leaves them in the DB (each has 1 auto-created profile + up to 1 TEST_guest_item + 1 TEST_guest_outfit). These are lightweight and self-expiring (session_token TTL 7 days). One TEST_second-profile attempt was blocked by 402 so no extra profile leaked. UI test also created 1 guest user per manual login. Consider periodic cleanup: db.users.deleteMany({is_guest:true, created_at:{$lt: <>}) + cascade to profiles/items/outfits/user_sessions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Guest Mode is stable. To resume-test: mint fresh guest with `curl -X POST $BASE/api/auth/guest` → stash session_token as Bearer, or via UI tap [data-testid=guest-login-button] on /login. Feature testIDs: login screen — google-login-button, guest-login-button, login-screen; Profile — guest-backup-cta (guest-only), logout-button (hidden for guests). Guest tokens are prefixed 'guest_' so they're easy to distinguish. Free-limits: {stylist:5/day, beauty:1/month}; all other AI = Premium-only. Test seed: mobile viewport 390x844, EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL https://wardrobe-ai-311.preview.emergentagent.com. Real Google OAuth NOT automatable — assert /auth/session behaviour via the seeded token test-session-token-aura-123 (user_testaura01) or invalid tokens.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Everything the request asked us to validate works end-to-end.
